themes.title: Anthropic post-IPO: models cheaper, greenshoe questioned
themes.summary: Anthropic closed its IPO with the underwriters' greenshoe fully exercised, then shipped a new Claude family — Opus 5.5 costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 and leads agentic coding, while Haiku 5.5 targets high-volume subagents and browser use. FT raises questions about the greenshoe timing after share-price weakness, and The Neuron tallies founders selling nearly $2B while Amazon and Google still hold the larger stakes.
themes.angle: Frontier inference just got ~40% cheaper at the same time the AI trade is repricing — boards should recheck their unit economics.

themes.title: Global AI trade sell-off reprices the boom
themes.summary: Equities are repricing the AI trade across the Americas and Asia: Korea slid more than 3% after heavy Wall Street losses, emerging-market stocks are set to erase their 2026 gains, and Reuters argues an AI bust would hurt Chinese stocks far more than GDP. The Information frames the moment as a bubble test for enterprise AI vendors with Dell and Workday reporting next.
themes.angle: The first real stress test of the AI capex thesis — watch earnings, not headlines.

themes.title: Gulf states move AI from pilot to programme
themes.summary: Dubai's State of AI report counts 90+ AI applications deployed across 20 government entities, Saudi digital transformation has crossed 90% with SAR 26bn in annual savings, and Riyadh has signed an AI-technology cooperation pact with Bulgaria. The UAE is also exporting its 1M AI-coders programme to the Dominican Republic and deepening AI research ties through MBZUAI and the Dubai Future Foundation.
themes.angle: Gulf governments are publishing adoption numbers, not just ambitions — the strongest regional signal in months.

themes.title: AI-powered cyber threats reach the boardroom
themes.summary: Axios's survey of 50+ leaders across government, AI, business and cyber found unanimity: attacks on business and critical infrastructure will be constant, increasingly sophisticated and AI-amplified. themes.title: AI governance: limits, states, and a packed December
themes.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist is proposing that leading AI firms agree to limit development of ever-more-powerful models until behaviour is better understood, while a bipartisan group of US governors wants federal rules that keep state consumer, worker and child protections intact. Congress heads into a December dense with AI policy fights.
themes.angle: Capability-limits talk plus state-vs-federal friction: the regulatory dial is moving faster than most boards assume.

themes.title: Chip export squeeze and data-centre cost inflation
themes.summary: Washington's post-Nvidia chip crackdown on China is squeezing Southeast Asia's multibillion-dollar cloud business, while Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are raising AI server prices by up to 45% months after contracts were signed. The Information argues Amazon's capital endurance is what neocloud rivals can't match.
themes.angle: Export rules and mid-contract price hikes are quietly rewriting who can build — and what AI infrastructure costs.
